It is my absolute pleasure to welcome you to Newlands Primary Academy. We opened our brand new school in September 2025. At Newlands, we are setting out on an exciting journey to create a vibrant, nurturing, and inspiring learning community where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to thrive.
As the founding Headteacher, I am proud to lead a school built on strong values and high aspirations. Our mission is to develop confident, compassionate, and curious learners who are not only well-prepared academically but also equipped with the skills and character to flourish in the wider world.
Our passionate and dedicated team is committed to delivering a broad, engaging, and inclusive curriculum that captures children’s interests and ignites a lifelong love of learning. From the very start, we will offer rich learning experiences both inside and outside the classroom—including outdoor learning, local exploration, and opportunities to connect with nature.
At Newlands Primary Academy, we believe in the power of partnership. We are excited to build strong, supportive relationships with parents, carers, and the wider community to ensure every child receives the very best start to their educational journey.
I warmly invite you to explore our website and discover more about the vision and values that will shape our new school. If you are considering Newlands for your child, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit and share in the exciting future ahead.
Kind regards,Mrs Jennifer ThorntonHeadteacher

sports premium
At Newlands Primary Academy, we believe that physical education should be an essential part of every child’s school experiences, and we promote daily physical well-being for every learner.
Physical education develops children’s knowledge, skills and understanding, so that they can perform with increasing skill and confidence in a range of physical activities. These include dance, games, gymnastics, athletics and outdoor activities. Physical education promotes an understanding in children of their bodies in action and the skills of cooperation, teamwork and respect. It promotes positive attitudes towards a healthy lifestyle for their future. We are fortunate to have, in our school grounds, an excellent environment for outdoor physical education.
We welcome the government’s commitment to sport in primary schools through the School Sport Premium. This funding is given to schools to promote physical exercise and well-being for children. At Newlands Primary Academy decisions are made each year to ensure that this funding is used to improve our provision for PE, and to improve the quality of the PE and sport activities we can offer their pupils. The impact of this funding is reviewed each year, and details of these will be available to view on this page of our website when available. We aim to ensure that these improvements are sustainable, by linking them with staff development, resource provision and raised expectations and aspirations for all our children.

English - reading
At Newlands Primary Academy, reading is at the heart of our curriculum. We believe that reading is the key to unlocking learning across all subjects and is fundamental to children’s future success. Our aim is to develop confident, fluent and enthusiastic readers who enjoy reading for both pleasure and purpose.
We teach phonics through the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised phonics programme. Through daily, systematic phonics lessons, children learn the knowledge and skills needed to become accurate and fluent readers, while regular reading practice sessions help to develop confidence, fluency and comprehension.
We teach reading using the CUSP Reading curriculum, which is built around high-quality, ambitious texts. Through explicit teaching of vocabulary, reading fluency and comprehension, pupils develop a deep understanding of what they read and learn to think critically about a wide range of literature. The carefully sequenced curriculum enables children to build their knowledge, language and understanding over time, ensuring strong progression throughout their primary years.
We foster a love of reading by exposing children to a rich range of books, authors, poets and genres, helping every pupil to see themselves as a reader and develop a lifelong enjoyment of literature.
Our expectation is that all of our children read at home with families at least four times a week and record this on Boom Reader.
Drawing Club Statement
Reading Curriculum Statement

Religious Education
At Newlands Primary Academy, Religious Education is taught through the Hampshire Living Difference IV syllabus. RE provides children with opportunities to explore beliefs, values, practices and ways of life from a range of religions and worldviews, helping them to understand the diverse society in which they live.
Using the Living Difference cycle of enquiry, children investigate important concepts and questions, encouraging them to think deeply, ask meaningful questions and reflect on their own experiences and beliefs. Through discussion, exploration and respectful debate, pupils learn to appreciate different perspectives while developing their own understanding of the world.
Our RE curriculum promotes curiosity, respect and open-mindedness. Children learn about a range of religions and worldviews, including Christianity and other principal faiths represented in Britain, exploring how beliefs influence the lives of individuals and communities.
Through Religious Education, we aim to develop thoughtful, respectful and informed learners who are equipped to engage positively with the diverse world around them and reflect on questions of meaning, purpose and identity.
Right to Withdraw from Religious Education (RE)
At Newlands Primary Academy, we are committed to providing an inclusive and enriching curriculum that helps every child grow in confidence, curiosity, and understanding of the wider world. As part of this, all pupils take part in Religious Education (RE), which supports their spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development.
We also recognise and respect that families hold a wide range of beliefs and values. In line with Section 71 of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998, parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education.
If you are considering withdrawing your child from RE, we warmly encourage you to speak with Mrs Thornton. This conversation helps ensure you have clear information about what RE looks like at Newlands and how it supports our wider aim of nurturing thoughtful, compassionate learners. Parents may withdraw their child without needing to give a reason, though we are always happy to talk through any questions.
Should you choose to proceed, the school will continue to supervise your child during RE lessons, although alternative curriculum teaching is not required. Pupils usually remain on site unless they are receiving suitable religious education elsewhere.
All requests should be made in writing to Mrs Thornton and will be recorded and reviewed annually.
At Newlands, we value our strong partnership with parents and carers, and we are always here to support you in making the right decisions for your child.

Pupil premium
Pupil Premium is an additional amount of funding allocated to schools by the government which is additional to main school funding, is the best way to address the inequalities between children eligible for free school meals (FSM), looked after children & service children and other pupils. Three categories of children are eligible:
Children who are eligible for the pupil premium need to be aged 4 and over, in year groups to year 11 in a maintained school.
It is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium is spent and they will be held accountable for how this additional funding is impacting on those for whom the money is allocated. The government thinks that schools are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for individual pupils within their responsibility. However all schools will be held accountable for how they have used additional funding to support pupils from low-income families and in care. The schools must report and publicise annually how the money has been spent and what the impact has been made on the achievements of the pupils.
Children who are eligible for Pupil Premium may experience many different barriers to educational achievement. Teachers assess the learning and development needs of all children and share these regularly with parents and carers. For children who are eligible for Pupil Premium, these are recorded each half term along with current measures and provision that are in place to enable every child to make the best possible progress.
The impact of the use made of this additional funding is under constant review, and is formally assessed at the end of each academic year.
If you think you may be eligible for pupil premium funding, please apply online at Free school meals | Education and learning | Hampshire County Council

Music
At Newlands Primary Academy, we teach Music through the Charanga Music Scheme, which provides a creative, engaging and progressive curriculum for all children. Music is a universal language, and we aim to inspire a love of music while developing confidence, creativity and a sense of achievement.
Through Charanga, pupils develop their skills in listening, singing, performing, improvising, composing and appraising music. Children explore a wide range of musical styles, genres and traditions, learning to recognise and understand the different elements of music, including pulse, rhythm, pitch, tempo and structure.
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced to ensure progression from Early Years through to Year 6. Through practical musical experiences, children build their knowledge and skills over time, developing as confident performers, thoughtful listeners and creative composers. Opportunities to work collaboratively, perform to others and use musical technology further enhance learning and enjoyment.
We believe that every child is musical. Through a rich and inspiring curriculum, we aim to nurture a lifelong appreciation of music and encourage all pupils to express themselves creatively and confidently.
Newlands Music Development Plan

Curriculum Statement
At Newlands Primary Academy, it is our intention to support our children to become lifelong learners; who have the knowledge and skill to be successful at the next stage of their educational journey.
We implement this through a carefully sequenced curriculum and appropriate learning journeys to meet the needs of our learners. We involve you in this process through our home learning requests and parental workshops. Our parent information sheets help you to understand what we are teaching each half-term so that you can have valuable discussions at home.
The impact of this is the progress that your children make - the knowledge and understanding that they can apply to their learning and the recall that they have to be successful in their learning and within society.
As a school and community we have created a vision for Newlands Learners, which links closely to the values and aims of the University of Chichester Academy Trust.
This journey starts in the Early Years. We use the 'Reception Baseline Assessment' to help identify accurate starting points when children join us. This information is then used to inform curriculum planning so that children are challenged in their learning. Adults in EYFS support children to learn through a range of indoor and outdoor learning opportunities. There is a combination of adult led activities each day and continuous provision (Discovery Time).

Personal Development
At Newlands Primary Academy, personal development is at the heart of our vision for every child. We are committed to helping pupils grow into confident, resilient, respectful and responsible young people who are well prepared for life beyond primary school.
Through our curriculum, assemblies, enrichment opportunities and wider school experiences, children develop important life skills, learn about themselves and others, and gain an understanding of the world around them. We promote positive relationships, emotional wellbeing, British Values, equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring that all children feel valued and respected.
Our pupils are encouraged to take on responsibilities, contribute to the school community and develop leadership skills through a range of opportunities. Educational visits, clubs, visitors and special events further enrich learning and help children discover new interests and talents.
We believe that successful learners are also confident individuals and responsible citizens. By nurturing character, wellbeing and aspirations alongside academic achievement, we support every child to thrive both now and in the future.

English - writing
At Newlands Primary Academy, we believe that every child should develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to become a successful writer. Through the CUSP Writing curriculum, children learn to write for a range of purposes and audiences, developing their ability to communicate clearly, creatively and effectively.
Our writing curriculum is built around high-quality texts, rich vocabulary and carefully sequenced learning. Children explore a wide variety of genres, including narrative, poetry, reports, explanations, letters and persuasive writing, enabling them to understand the features and purpose of different forms of writing.
Vocabulary development is a key feature of our approach. Through explicit teaching, discussion and reading, children acquire ambitious vocabulary that enhances both their understanding and their written work. Grammar, punctuation and spelling are taught within meaningful contexts, helping pupils to apply their knowledge confidently and accurately.
As writers, children are encouraged to plan, draft, edit and improve their work, developing independence, resilience and pride in their achievements. By the time they leave Newlands Primary Academy, we aim for all pupils to be articulate, imaginative and confident writers who are equipped with the skills they need for the next stage of their education and beyond.

Maths
At Newlands Primary Academy, we teach mathematics using the NCETM Teaching for Mastery approach, which enables all children to develop a deep, secure and long-lasting understanding of mathematical concepts. We believe that every child can achieve success in mathematics through high-quality teaching, careful sequencing and appropriate challenge.
Lessons are designed to build understanding step by step, ensuring children develop fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills alongside conceptual understanding. Through whole-class teaching, pupils explore mathematical ideas together, using discussion, practical resources and visual representations to help them make connections and deepen their thinking.
Our mastery curriculum is underpinned by the NCETM’s Five Big Ideas: coherence, representation and structure, mathematical thinking, fluency and variation. These principles help children understand not only how mathematics works, but why it works, giving them the confidence to apply their knowledge in a range of contexts.
Through our mathematics curriculum, we aim to develop resilient, confident and enthusiastic mathematicians who can reason, explain and solve problems effectively, preparing them for future learning and everyday life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Newlands Primary Academy - Assessment and Reporting
pageCache.text:
Assessment and Reporting
Teachers are continuously assessing children in lots of ways. In classes, children answer questions, teachers observe the learning and review work. All of these aspects of classroom life support the teachers in understanding what the children know and what they need to help them move on in their learning.
Within books and through evaluation of their work, children are involved in their own assessments. This helps them to understand how successful they have been and to identify their next steps. Doing this helps them to take control of their learning and develop as independent, lifelong learners.

Awards and Partnerships
School Readers
Schoolreaders recruits, places and supports volunteers in local primary schools to give children one-to-one reading support on a weekly basis. We're proud to be a partner school, able to provide our pupils with this valuable extra time each week!

pageCache.pageTitle: Newlands Primary Academy - design and technology
pageCache.text:
design and technology
At Newlands Primary Academy, we teach Design and Technology through the Projects on a Page scheme, developed by the Design & Technology Association. This engaging and progressive curriculum enables children to become creative problem-solvers, designers and innovators by designing, making and evaluating products for real purposes and audiences.
Children develop their knowledge and skills across a range of areas including structures, mechanisms, textiles, food and nutrition, and electrical systems. Through practical, hands-on projects, pupils learn to investigate existing products, generate and communicate ideas, select and use appropriate tools and materials, and evaluate their outcomes to improve their designs.
The curriculum is carefully sequenced to ensure progression in both technical knowledge and design skills as children move through the school. By encouraging creativity, resilience and critical thinking, Design and Technology helps pupils understand how products are developed and equips them with the confidence and skills to shape the world around them.
